summary: Approval request becomes irrecoverably locked when Okta session rotates during one-time approval token issuance
summary_long: A short-lived approval token generated during an internal access request (support console) becomes invalid if the requestor's Okta session rotates mid-flow. The approval entry remains in a locked state and cannot be re-opened by admins or the requestor, blocking several oncall runbooks.
impact: Multiple oncall engineers unable to re-open pending access requests to run critical incident playbooks; manual workarounds required (Slack approvals + ticketing), increasing MTTR for active incidents.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a support console access request for runbook elevation (devops-runner) from a user with an existing Okta session.
2) Admin clicks approve in the console which triggers generation of a one-time approval token sent to Okta approval webhook.
3) Simulate Okta session rotation for the requester (force refresh or IdP reissue) while webhook processing is in-flight.
4) Observe approval endpoint returning 401 for token verification and the console request flips to an intermediate 'locked' state with no retry path.
5) Attempts to cancel/reopen from console, or to reissue approval, result in 'token already consumed' or 'request locked' errors.
observed_behavior: Approval token verification fails with 401/invalid-assertion during IdP session rotation. Console shows locked request with no action buttons. Admins cannot re-issue approval; requestor cannot re-submit without creating a new request (which duplicates queue entries).
expected_behavior: If token verification fails due to IdP session churn, the approval flow should either re-queue the request for retry or expose a clear admin action to reissue a new token without duplicating entries.

investigation_notes: Token model: one-time JWT tied to Okta session claim (sid). If sid mismatch -> 401 and token marked consumed.
Race window: ~600ms between token creation and Okta session reissue can cause verification failure for legitimate approvals when IdP refreshes device context.
Approval-queue currently marks request terminal on 401 to avoid replay attacks; that policy lacks a retry backoff for transient IdP churn.
We confirmed reproducer in prod-us-east with synthetic requests hitting the same auth-proxy path used by console approvals.
No existing linked incident on status.redwood.com; limited to internal console workflows but high operational impact.
temporary_workarounds: Manual: Admins can ask approver to re-initiate approval from console after invalidation; this creates duplicate queue entries but unblocks runbook.
Short-term patch: Auth team can run a one-off DB script to flip locked requests back to 'awaiting_approval' for specific request IDs (risky; requires audit log).
Operational: For active incidents, escalate in #support and perform Slack-based approvals with a manual audit entry until fix lands.
next_steps: 1) Implement change in approval-queue: treat 401 due to session mismatch as retryable for a short window (configurable 5s) and do not mark request terminal immediately.
2) Add explicit admin action in console to 'reissue approval token' which triggers a safe reattempt without duplicating requests.
3) Add telemetry to track frequency of session-rotation-induced verification failures and signal to IdP team if rate high.
4) Run canary of patch in staging, then us-east prod for low-traffic orgs before global rollout.
5) Write a short runbook describing manual mitigation steps for oncall.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-15 02:30 UTC - Deploy candidate patch that classifies 'invalid-assertion' from session-rotate as retryable for 10s and surfaces admin 'reissue' button in console UI.
Post-deploy verification: Reproducer run against staging no longer produced locked state; prod canary (us-east) saw 0 locked events over 24h period after rollout.
Follow-up: Auth and platform added metrics (approval.token.failures_by_reason) and a monthly review for IdP churn patterns.
Long-term: Plan to remove sid-binding for one-time approval tokens and instead use short-lived nonce stored server-side to avoid coupling to Okta session churn.
